title_he: כִּי פָדִיתָ אוֹתִי וּקְנִיתָנִי, הוֹי מוֹשִׁיעִי הַנֶּהְדָּר
review: 1:1–4 is the printed four-line acclamation with the verb repeated three times, as the Arabic repeats اِجْذِبْنِي; the Hebrew keeps the repetition on מָשְׁכֵנִי rather than varying to 'draw near', because the stanza's force is the repeated pull (Song 1:4, מָשְׁכֵנִי אַחֲרֶיךָ).

3:2 בְּהִתְיַחֲדִי עִם־אֲדֹנִי — the Arabic إِذْ بِرَبِّي أَخْتَلِي is 'when I am alone with my Lord'; הִתְיַחֵד is the biblical verb for being set apart (Exod 29:43, נוֹעַד), so 'alone with' keeps its sense of a private appointed meeting rather than mere solitude.
3:3 נִקְצֹר עֹנֶג — the Arabic نَجْتَنِي الْهَنَا is 'we reap bliss'; the harvest verb is kept (Lev 25:11, קָצַר), so conversation with the Lord is pictured as reaping.

4:1 חָנֵּנִי וְקַדְּשֵׁנִי לָךְ — the Arabic جُدْ وَكَرِّسْنِي لَكَ خَصِّصْنِي is three imperatives ('bestow, consecrate, appoint'); the Hebrew keeps three acts but compresses the last two into קַדֵּשׁ + לָךְ, since a fourth imperative overruns the tune's ten syllables.
5:2 לֹא אֶשַּׂג — the Arabic لَا أَعِي is 'I do not grasp/comprehend'; the Hebrew uses the Hiphil of נשׂג as in Ps 139:6 (לֹא אוּכַל), so the line is about comprehension failing, not memory.
